proposals.text: A shopper must not take a cart into a single-file aisle flanked by shelves on both sides.
proposals.justification: The rule depends on local aisle geometry and shelf adjacency, so it applies to any layout with narrow shelf aisles rather than to named cells.

proposals.text: If a shopper parks or releases a cart, they should do so only in an open staging area rather than beside shelves or in a constricted passage.
proposals.justification: The notion of an open staging area is defined by local clearance and absence of adjacent shelves, not by a particular store coordinate.

proposals.text: After parking a cart, the shopper is obliged to retrieve a cart before leaving.
proposals.justification: Retrieving a cart one has parked is a general shopping practice independent of where the parking place is located.

proposals.text: When a shopper enters a single-file shelf aisle without a cart, they are obliged to perform the shelf interaction there before returning.
proposals.justification: The rule refers to entering a locally identified narrow shelf aisle, so it generalizes across stores with different aisle positions.

proposals.text: After interacting with a shelf while away from the cart, the shopper is obliged to regain a cart before exit.
proposals.justification: The trigger is defined by the shopper's cart status and adjacency to any shelf, not by a particular shelf location.

proposals.text: A shopper must not leave the store without a cart.
proposals.justification: The constraint concerns the general exit action and cart possession, which are meaningful in every store layout.

proposals.text: From the start of the trip, the shopper is obliged to acquire a cart before completing the shopping trajectory.
proposals.justification: The rule captures a domain-level expectation to use a cart and does not depend on where the cart station is placed.

proposals.text: When not holding a cart, a shopper may move only within open staging areas or single-file shelf aisles.
proposals.justification: The allowed off-cart areas are characterized by local geometry and shelf relations, making the rule transferable to different floor plans.

The demonstrations are now shown in a lower-level representation that exposes distinctions hidden before (newly available: geometry). Identify the hidden distinctions and use them to define higher-level state properties and/or events (in "abstraction"), possibly hierarchically, and propose norms expressed over them. Norms may also use the primitive atoms directly.
Generalisation requirement. Some candidate rules merely describe the particular store in which the demonstrations were recorded -- for example rules that mention specific coordinates, cells or regions of this floor plan. Such rules can fit the demonstrations without capturing the social norm, and would be meaningless in a store with a different floor plan. Distinguish (a) candidate norms that express general behavioural constraints of the shopping domain from (b) rules that only describe the geometry or coordinates of this particular environment. Propose candidates of type (a): define any abstractions from layout-independent relations rather than from coordinates (at(x,y)), so that the same rule could be applied unchanged in any store layout. Every candidate must still be consistent with all demonstrations. Add a field "justification" (one sentence) to each element explaining why the rule remains meaningful across different store layouts.
Propose 8 diverse candidate hypotheses.

Output format: return ONLY a JSON list (no prose, no code fences). Each element:
{"id": short_name, "text": one-sentence natural-language statement of the norm,
 "abstraction": {"state_properties": {name: FORMULA, ...},
                 "events": {name: {"pre": FORMULA, "post": FORMULA or null}, ...}},
 "norm": {"type": "prohibition", "condition": FORMULA}
       | {"type": "obligation", "trigger": FORMULA or "START", "discharge": FORMULA}}
FORMULA := atom | name of a property/event defined in this hypothesis | {"not": F} | {"and": [F, ...]}
         | {"or": [F, ...]} | {"le"|"lt"|"ge"|"gt"|"eq": [numeric_feature, integer]}
Semantics.  A trajectory is a sequence of steps (state s_k, action a_k).  A step's label contains the atoms true in
s_k and the action a_k.  A state property is a formula over state atoms (no actions).  An event
{"pre": P, "post": Q} occurs at step k when P holds for the label of step k and Q holds in the next state s_{k+1}
(post may be null).  A prohibition counts one violation for every step whose label (including events occurring at
that step) satisfies the condition.  An obligation becomes pending at any step satisfying the trigger ("START" =
pending from the beginning) and is fulfilled by a later (or the same) step satisfying the discharge; it can be
triggered again; it is violated if it is still pending when the trajectory ends.

parsed.justification: The notion of an open staging area is defined by local clearance and absence of adjacent shelves, not by a particular store coordinate.

parsed.text: After parking a cart, the shopper is obliged to retrieve a cart before leaving.
parsed.justification: Retrieving a cart one has parked is a general shopping practice independent of where the parking place is located.

parsed.text: After interacting with a shelf while away from the cart, the shopper is obliged to regain a cart before exit.

parsed.text: A shopper must not leave the store without a cart.
